rule: Layers are ordered low to high (WP-06/WP-07 order, F2_memory_core_contract.md section 1.2). A unit may import units of the same or a LOWER layer only. Facade packages are `aliases`, not layers: an import through a facade is an edge to the unit that owns the submodule (first match in the facade's declared __path__), and the real __path__ of every alias must equal the declared one. An upward edge is allowed only while it is listed in baseline_edges. hard_forbidden (package -> product, also through an alias) is enforced even when the edge no longer goes up. The check is a ratchet: new upward edges and growth fail, and so does a stale baseline (edge removed or count lower), so every gain must be locked by regenerating the baseline. Edge count = number of non-test files of the source unit importing the target unit. Non-test imports include `-m` argv lists in .py files inside a unit, and test-path files imported by production code. Non-literal import_module/__import__ calls are counted per unit in baseline_dynamic_imports (same ratchet semantics).
unenforced: Facade resolution follows the declared/real __path__ and the re-export line of root cognitive_core/<mod>.py (`from [packages.]X.<m> import *`); a facade submodule no __path__ entry serves keeps the edge on the facade, is listed in the inventory meta.facade_unresolved and FAILS the check (i) when the file is non-test.

`security.X` from the repository root is root/security; packages/security records its extended __path__ (self, root/security) but does not change how `security` resolves. The name collision itself is WP-14.
Layer membership of an alias (facade) is not checked: an edge to an unresolved facade is only judged by hard_forbidden.
Non-literal dynamic imports are counted per unit, not resolved to a target unit.
Reassigning a unit to another layer in this config is caught only by diff review.
Relative imports and same-directory sys.path imports are not resolved.
python -m strings in non-.py files inside a unit are not edges (only py_argv_m and python_c).
R1 (WP-04 review r2): `-c` argv in .py files ([sys.executable, '-c', 'import x']) is not parsed; python_c is read only from shell/yml-type files.
R2: shell command strings inside .py files (os.system('python -m x'), subprocess with shell=True) are not scanned.
R3: import_module aliased by assignment (im = importlib.import_module), getattr(importlib, 'import_module') and builtins.__import__ are not counted.
R4: transitive edges through .py files outside any unit (e.g. 03_IMPLEMENTATION/x.py) are not followed.

R7 (WP-07 PR A review r2): __path__ changed through an obfuscated reference (an alias such as `_p = __path__; _p.append(...)`, setattr on the module, globals()['__path__']) is not detected; same class as R3, caught only by diff review. A plain `import <facade>` without a submodule in non-test code fails check (j).

L2 (WP-07 PR A review): the re-export follow for a facade's own modules (`cognitive_core/<mod>.py` of a facade that lists `self`) is a regex heuristic on `from [packages.]X.<m> import *`; an unusual re-export spelling keeps the edge on the facade (then reported in meta.facade_unresolved and failed by check (i)).

A `__path__` move outside the unit's own __init__.py (e.g. `memory_controller.__path__.insert(...)` in another file) is listed in the inventory `unknown` but is not parsed or failed by the layer check; only the __init__ of a unit is evaluated.

R5/R6 (low): a mixed refuse+tighten --write-baseline run writes the tightening and exits 1; --owner-wp format is not validated; a trailing '# python -m x' comment still yields a string ref; 'python -malpha' and 'pypy3 -m' are missed.

excluded.test_files: Files matching package_inventory.is_test_path (under 20_TESTS/ or tests/, named test_*.py, or conftest.py) are not counted.

hard_forbidden.rule: A package-kind unit must never import a product-kind unit, directly or through the packages/xau_kinetic alias.

aliases_note: Facades are __path__ shims, not layers: an import through one is an edge to the unit that serves the submodule (first match in __path__). `__path__` is the declared, ordered list of units; "self" = the shim's own directory. The check fails if the real __path__ (package_inventory shim_targets) differs.
